key_insight: LeanPRM turns Lean-formalized proofs into step-level supervision for natural-language proof verification without human annotations.
engineering_relevance: It provides a scalable recipe for training proof verifiers that can improve step checking and best-of-N proof selection across model sizes.
method: Generate a natural-language proof and a paired Lean formal proof without Lean feedback.
Use Lean to label each proof step as correct or incorrect.
Filter out syntax-only Lean failures with a second model so negatives reflect mathematical mistakes.
evidence_signal: The dataset includes 10,634 proofs and 152K labeled steps; a Qwen3-4B verifier improved exact step-label accuracy on LeanPRM-Bench from 48.2% to 74.7% and beat PRM800K training at 60.3%.
watch_item: The pipeline depends on the availability and quality of formal Lean statements and on a secondary model to separate syntactic failures from genuine math errors.
paper_title: LeanPRM: Lean-Grounded Process Supervision for Natural Language Proof Verification
